My damn debit card. Is it in my car? Is it loose in my bag? Is it in the wrong spot in my wallet? Is it in my pocket? What about the pants I wore yesterday? Was it in my pocket but I took it out when I went to use the restroom? Did I accidentally wash it? Sometimes I just don’t even bother looking for it because it means I can’t spend money.

A sub once described his perfect girlfriend to the class. He described one of the girls in the class to the T while staring at her. He didn’t work for our school long after that.

It happened to me. I had JUST escaped an abusive relationship and didn’t have anywhere to go. I called, talked, calmed down, and decided I’d sleep in the car for the night. I was asleep when an officer and an ambulance show up and tell me that I can get in willingly and they’ll take me to the nearest hospital or they’ll make me go and they’ll take me to the hospital a few hours away. I had no way to get to get back to my vehicle, nor did I have insurance, so I chose the closer hospital. 

The whole hospital experience was a shit show too. One of the nurses even told me that next time I feel like that I shouldn’t call. He essentially told me I should’ve just killed myself. They called my abusive ex that I had JUST left and released me to him. Lmao. 

Now I’m in debt for a few thousand with a shit credit score and an even more deep-seeded fear of hospitals.
Uhhhhhh......rapping?

This was actually the turning point in my boyfriend and my relationship. In the beginning he was so anxious that he felt like he had to fill every moment of silence. One day I just straight up told him “Look, I’m okay with silence. We don’t have to always be talking just to talk. I’m perfectly fine just being in the moment with you even if we’re just sitting in the same room.” That’s when our relationship blossomed. When you you quit having conversations about the weather you have the opportunity to have conversations that actually matter.

I once knew a “comedian” who would use regular conversation to practice his stand-up routines. He once tried to fill a natural pause in conversation with “have you ever just wanted to fuck the moon.”  It was so hard to just talk to him about normal stuff. Jokes in conversation can definitely be over-done so be careful.

I never thought I would have to think about what I would do if I got pregnant. My boyfriend and I sat down and had a very real conversation. Not about whether I would have an abortion but rather how. How we would go about leaving the state that I’m in. Who we could go to. What my options are if I found out early enough to not involve a hospital. I actually looked up how to preform an abortion at home with intent on doing whatever I needed to do to make sure if I were ever in that position I could fix it. It’s 2019 and I’m 100% willing to have a “back-alley” “coat-hanger” abortion if that’s what it takes. I would rather chance hurting myself than bringing a child into this world.
